v1.feedback: The sonar-ping concept maps well to the word 'ping' and delivers a genuine tonal swerve (cyan digital pulse through warm vascular geometry), but the differential growth core is inherited nearly verbatim from cyx — the 'surprise' lives almost entirely in the ping overlay rather than reshaping the underlying form. To strengthen: modulate the growth parameters themselves when a ping fires (e.g., temporarily spike REPEL_STR or RISE near the wavefront so the tower physically flinches), and consider tightening the camera or raising fog density so the tower fills more frame — at camera distance 14 with fog 0.04 the upper growth risks fading into background before it reads.

v2.feedback: The sonar-ping wavefront is a genuine surprise swerve — it physically deforms the differential-growth tower and the cyan flash reads clearly against the warm vascular palette. Two things to push: the tube radii (0.03–0.045) are thin enough that at default camera distance the form can read as wispy lines rather than fleshy vasculature — doubling them would strengthen the silhouette. Second, the ping's visual payoff is mostly the shader tint band; adding a brief emissive ring geometry or a radial particle burst at the wavefront would make the 'flinch' moment more dramatic and justify the compute the physics modulation is already doing.
